source.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
source.authors: Rohan Gupta; Iv'an Arcuschin; Thomas Kwa; Adrià Garriga-Alonso

record.tranche_reason: The study applies resample ablation, the intervention used to assess the IOI circuit, to GPT-2 small and reports node effects on IOI prompts. Its analysis is limited to node-wise effects rather than the full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation.
record.gate_note: The IOI-specific results are in Section C and Table 7/Figure 17. The paper analyzes 10,000 samples using the exact circuit ACDC used as ground truth. It reports node-effect statistics for circuit and non-circuit nodes, and separately notes a Layer 0 MLP effect of 0.999. It does not report the result of ablating all nodes outside the circuit together, nor test backup heads, other models, or prompt variants. Results for SIIT models on other tasks and the circuit-discovery-method benchmark do not directly test these IOI claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix C resample-ablates each node of GPT-2 small on 10,000 IOI prompts. It compares the share of changed top outputs for nodes inside and outside the ACDC ground-truth IOI circuit. This bears on whether the circuit captures the behaviour (V1 faithfulness and completeness; V5 partial explanation). The method is a single-node output-flip measure rather than Wang et al.'s whole-circuit logit-difference criteria, so T2, not T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report that some nodes outside the GPT-2 small IOI circuit have higher resample-ablation effects than some inside, and that in-circuit effects are much lower than in SIIT models. They suggest the circuit is more spread out or redundant. They flag MLP0 (effect 0.999) as problematic because of its unclear label. They use this to argue that manually found circuits like IOI lack ground truth and are 'not completely faithful', which motivates InterpBench.
record.recipe_differences: Uses resample ablation on GPT-2 small and the IOI circuit, but reports node-effect distributions rather than validating faithfulness, completeness, and minimality as a whole.

fits_no_version.finding: The SIIT semi-synthetic 6-layer model trained to implement a simplified IOI circuit shows clean separation. In-circuit node effects have quartiles 0.86-0.99-1.00 and out-of-circuit effects are about 0.00 under resample and mean ablation (Tables 1-2). The circuit is imposed by training, so this does not test whether GPT-2 or other natural models use it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A simplified IOI circuit (duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover roles) can be implemented faithfully in a small transformer trained with SIIT.

record.problems: The IOI analysis reports node-wise effects, not the effect of jointly ablating everything outside the circuit. It uses the same IOI dataset used to train the semi-synthetic model (10,000 samples); the paper does not state a separate GPT-2 small performance baseline. The authors identify Layer 0 MLP's circuit label as unclear.
record.rows_left_out: None of the IOI-specific node-effect results were left out. Other-task SIIT ablation results and circuit-discovery comparisons are not rows because they do not evaluate the GPT-2 small IOI circuit.

untested.parts: The 26-head count, the 7 classes and their roles, and the whole-circuit faithfulness, completeness and minimality metrics. Only single-node ablation effects are reported.
All: no ablation of name movers and no measurement of backup takeover.
All: only GPT-2 small is analysed. The SIIT IOI model is trained to implement the circuit.
All for GPT-2 small IOI. The method comparisons are on SIIT Tracr models only.
Dependence on ablation type, metric or prompt distribution for GPT-2 small IOI. Only resample ablation and the flip metric are used.
All: no name-order, template or more-names variants.

record.verdict_notes: The tranche is changed from T1 to T2: the measure is a per-node argmax-flip rate, not the original whole-circuit faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests. The reader's 'challenges' label for V1 on R2/R3 is dropped. R3's MLP0 effect is near-trivial under resample ablation and outside the head-only circuit's scope. R2 shows overlap, not absence of separation, which fits limits_scope. The IOI analysis is an appendix side result in a benchmark paper.

versions.untested_parts: Tests node-wise resample-ablation effects against the proposed circuit labels. Does not independently validate the 26-head count, all seven classes and their roles, or the full faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Does not ablate main name-mover heads or test takeover by backup heads.
Does not test the IOI circuit in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics on the GPT-2 small IOI circuit.
Reports node-wise resample-ablation effects and evidence that the circuit is incomplete or has redundancies. Does not compare ablation types, metrics, or prompt distributions on GPT-2 small IOI.
Does not test other name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablate individual nodes and measure the proportion of outputs changed; aggregate for nodes labeled in the IOI circuit.
rows.note: The mean node effect is low, and the range includes nodes with substantially greater effects. Authors say the overall effect is lower than for SIIT models and may indicate a more spread-out circuit or redundancies.
rows.check: In-circuit nodes have a mean effect of 0.028, about 3x the out-of-circuit mean of 0.009. Absolute effects are tiny, though: median 0.014, minimum 0.001. The measure is the proportion of argmax flips from ablating one node. It is insensitive to redundancy and is not the original logit-difference faithfulness. No unablated baseline is needed, since the effect is a change rate. The prompts are the IOI dataset InterpBench used to train its SIIT model, which may differ from Wang et al.'s distribution.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix C; Table 7; Figure 17; Section 5.1 node-effect definition.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablate individual nodes and measure the proportion of outputs changed; aggregate for nodes labeled outside the IOI circuit.
rows.note: Although the aggregate effect is small, the authors state that some nodes outside the circuit have effects higher than some nodes inside it.
rows.check: Out-of-circuit nodes mostly have low effects: median 0.008, mean 0.009. Some reach 0.071, above the in-circuit median of 0.014 and upper quartile of 0.024. Separation from in-circuit nodes is therefore incomplete, not absent. The individual high-effect nodes are not identified.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix C; Table 7; Figure 17; Section 5.1 node-effect definition.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablate Layer 0 MLP; its effect is noted separately and excluded from the main analysis.
rows.note: The paper says Wang et al. did not study this node and the circuit used as ground truth does not label it as in-circuit; the authors call its label unclear and its effect high.
rows.check: Resample-ablating MLP0 with another prompt largely swaps the token-level (embedding-like) information, so a 0.999 flip rate is close to trivial. Wang et al.'s circuit is a set of attention heads and does not address MLP0; the authors themselves call its label unclear. This row cannot show whether the head circuit is incomplete. It is a single excluded node, not a circuit-level result.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI prompts, single-node resample ablation, argmax-flip metric (excluding MLP0)
relationships.reason: In-circuit nodes average higher effects (0.028 vs 0.009), but some out-of-circuit nodes reach 0.071, above most in-circuit nodes. The labelled circuit does not cleanly separate causally relevant nodes (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Circuit nodes averaged effects of 0.028 versus 0.009 outside the circuit, but some external nodes reached 0.071, exceeding most circuit nodes.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI prompts, single-node resample ablation, argmax-flip metric (excluding MLP0)
source_check.reason: R1 and R2 show overlapping causal effects: means 0.028 inside and 0.009 outside, with an outside maximum of 0.071 exceeding the inside upper quartile of 0.024. This qualifies circuit coverage without demonstrating that the circuit's effect is absent.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI prompts, single-node resample ablation
relationships.reason: Out-of-circuit nodes with effects exceeding in-circuit ones, and low, spread-out in-circuit effects, indicate the circuit explains only part of the behaviour. The authors read this as spread-out or redundant computation (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Some external nodes had larger effects than circuit nodes, whose small, dispersed effects suggested distributed or redundant computation.

source_check.reason: R1 and R2 establish effects outside the labelled circuit and low, distributed effects inside it. Appendix C suggests spread-out or redundant computation, supporting the partial-explanation component of V5.

relation.reason: The study directly measures causal effects inside and outside the GPT-2-small IOI circuit and interprets their overlap as evidence qualifying the circuit's coverage.

tranche.reason: Appendix C evaluates the published circuit using individual-node resampling and output-change distributions, a different measure from joint circuit faithfulness, completeness and minimality.

source_check.notes: Table 7 excludes MLP0, whose effect is 0.999; apply that exclusion to R2 as well. Its standard deviations describe variation across nodes, not uncertainty in the means; individual-node effects do not establish joint complement-ablation faithfulness or completeness.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small IOI samples under node-wise resample ablation
reader_labels.reason: A non-circuit Layer 0 MLP has a reported effect of 0.999, and some other nodes outside the circuit affect outputs more than some in-circuit nodes (R2, R3). This challenges the circuit’s faithfulness as labeled, without testing the full criteria.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Aggregate node-wise effects for in-circuit and out-of-circuit nodes
reader_labels.reason: The reported in-circuit mean effect is 0.028 and the out-of-circuit mean is 0.009, with overlapping ranges; this node-wise analysis does not establish the whole circuit’s claimed completeness or minimality (R1, R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small IOI samples under node-wise resample ablation
reader_labels.reason: The results suggest the proposed circuit is incomplete or redundant in this evaluation: some excluded nodes have high effects and out-of-circuit effects can exceed in-circuit effects (R1, R2, R3). Other ablations, metrics, and prompt distributions were not compared for this IOI analysis.
